why: Authored prose is text a human or a model WROTE ABOUT a page. It is not the page. A record whose text has an authored origin may be kept as a note, a roster or an eval fixture, but it may never become a page's embedding input, sparse surface, title or snippet -- and it may never be replayed by a rebuild as if it were the page's own content. This file is the one home for the list; code imports it (engineering-doctrine 1/4) instead of repeating the strings.
recorded: 2026-09-16. The origins below were found on the write path, not guessed: and both call persist_l1_records.write_l1_records with this exact origin string, and stamps it onto every record as `l1_origin`.

authored_manifests.note: 199 entries. Every `text` and `snippet` was written by a model on 2026-07-08/09 (tasks 106, 107b, 148) describing what the page says. `title` stays in the roster because it is the page's own title, not a claim about it; `text` and `snippet` do not.

stale_claim_note: A body that states a dated current-state fact ('the latest release is X, June 2026') is only true for as long as the fact is. 30 days is the bar a REFRESH must clear: a row whose newest dated claim is older than that has stopped describing the page and must be re-derived from a fetch, not re-embedded. Measured basis: 7 of 9 manifest claims spot-checked on 2026-09-16 were already false at ~10 weeks ().
